name: Recipient Passive with a Retained Object
pattern: Clause[Subject:recipient NP + passive be + V-en + retained theme NP]

entry.name: Recipient Passive with a Retained Object
entry.pattern: Clause[Subject:recipient NP + passive be + V-en + retained theme NP]

1.definition: Makes the recipient the passive subject while keeping the theme in object position.

examples.form: [A replacement key was sent to Lee].
examples.note: Constructed comparison. Theme subject with an oblique recipient.

relatedConstructions.notes: The recipient corresponds to the indirect object of the active frame.

projection.target: The replacement key remains an ordinary NP complement of sent. In A replacement key was sent to Lee, the theme instead controls agreement and the recipient is an oblique.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Being sent something
curious.summary: A passive sentence can make the person who receives something the subject while the thing received stays after the verb.
curious.body:
In Lee was sent a replacement key, Lee is the recipient and the subject of the sentence. The replacement key still sits after the verb, as an ordinary part of it.

Compare A replacement key was sent to Lee, where the key is the subject and Lee comes in a phrase with to. The two sentences describe the same sending but arrange the people and things differently. This dictionary marks the account as provisional.

examples.text: [A replacement key was sent to Lee].

curious.try: Turn Someone sent Lee a key into a sentence beginning with Lee, and then into one beginning with the key. How do the endings differ?

teacher.summary: Connects the passive of double-object verbs to the two ways of choosing the subject.
teacher.explain: The recipient becomes the passive subject while the theme stays in object position: Lee was sent a replacement key. The recipient corresponds to the indirect object of the active frame. The replacement key remains an ordinary NP complement of sent. In A replacement key was sent to Lee, the theme controls agreement and the recipient is an oblique. This dictionary marks the analysis provisional, and its examples are constructed.
teacher.terms: The remaining NP is sometimes called a retained object; this dictionary uses that term. See also the double-object (ditransitive) pattern.

contrasts.text: Lee was sent a replacement key.
contrasts.note: Recipient as subject; the theme is a retained object.

contrasts.text: A replacement key was sent to Lee.
contrasts.note: Theme as subject; recipient in a to-phrase.

watch_for: A learner might think the replacement key must be the subject because it is the thing sent.
A learner might look for a missing object after sent in the first sentence.
teacher.activity: Students start from Someone sent Lee a replacement key and write both passives, underlining the subject in each and saying what the other participant becomes.
